skill.name: runcomfy-cli
skill.description: Use the RunComfy CLI to authenticate, discover model inputs, submit media jobs, monitor requests, and download generated outputs.
skill.summary: Automate RunComfy model jobs from a terminal or script.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: All 118 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, safe shell examples, expected URLs, a placeholder ellipsis, standard token storage, or account inspection. A separate high-severity issue remains because the skill overstates shell-injection safety when agents may interpolate untrusted prompt text. Publication should wait until all user inputs use a file or structured JSON builder.

remediation.issue: The skill claims prompt content cannot create shell injection, but generated shell quoting can fail before the CLI receives the value.
remediation.suggestion: Require --input-file or a structured JSON builder for user-controlled values. Remove the absolute safety claim and prohibit direct interpolation into shell command text.

semantic_findings.title: Misleading Shell-Injection Assurance
semantic_findings.description: The skill states that prompt content has no shell-injection surface. Agent-generated commands can still interpolate untrusted text before the CLI receives it. Crafted quotes or shell syntax could escape the generated argument and execute another command.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 252 explicitly dismisses shell injection, while earlier examples construct shell arguments. The risk depends on how the agent quotes user-controlled prompt text.

content.value_statement: Running remote media models from scripts requires careful authentication, inputs, polling, and downloads. This skill provides practical RunComfy CLI workflows for those tasks.
actual_capabilities: Explains npm installation and interactive or token-based authentication.
Shows how to invoke RunComfy model endpoints with JSON or YAML inputs.
Supports synchronous runs, deferred polling, request status checks, and cancellation behavior.
Controls output directories, automatic downloads, and no-download responses.
Provides machine-readable output patterns for pipelines and batch jobs.
Documents exit codes and bounded retry handling for transient failures.
limitations: Requires a RunComfy account, valid credentials, the RunComfy CLI, and network access.
Does not provide every model schema; users must inspect the selected model API definition.
Remote jobs may incur charges, queue delays, timeouts, or provider failures.
User prompts and referenced media are processed by an external service.

use_cases.title: Create Media from a Terminal
use_cases.description: Submit one image or video request, monitor completion, and save the result in a chosen directory.

use_cases.title: Automate Application Assets
use_cases.description: Run repeatable model jobs from development scripts and consume machine-readable results.

use_cases.title: Process Prompt Batches
use_cases.description: Submit multiple prompts with unique output folders and bounded retries for temporary failures.

prompt_templates.title: Install and Sign In
prompt_templates.prompt: Install the RunComfy CLI with npm, help me authenticate interactively, verify my identity, and stop before sending any model request.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup on a local workstation

prompt_templates.title: Run One Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Run [model ID] with [input], save downloaded results in [directory], and explain the request status.

prompt_templates.title: Submit and Poll Later
prompt_templates.prompt: Submit [model ID] without waiting, return its request identifier, then show how to check status and download results later.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Resilient Batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a batch workflow for [prompt file] using safe JSON construction, unique output directories, machine-readable output, and bounded retries for transient errors.

output_examples.input: Generate one product image and save it in the campaign output directory.
output_examples.output: The model request completed successfully. One image was downloaded to the requested campaign directory.

output_examples.input: Submit a video job without waiting and provide the tracking information.
output_examples.output: The request was accepted for asynchronous processing. The response includes the request identifier needed for later status checks.

output_examples.input: Process a prompt list and retry only temporary service failures.
output_examples.output: Each prompt received a separate output directory. Temporary failures were retried with bounded backoff, while permanent errors stopped immediately.

best_practices: Inspect the selected model schema before building inputs.
Pass user-controlled values through an input file or structured JSON builder.
Protect tokens, use owner-only storage, and avoid logs or repository files.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe an unreviewed remote installer into a shell.
Do not ingest unrelated URLs or enable web search without explicit user need.
Do not retry permanent errors or create unbounded retry loops.

faq.question: What must be installed before using this skill?
faq.answer: Install the RunComfy CLI and provide a valid RunComfy account token.

faq.question: Can it run without an interactive browser?
faq.answer: Yes. CI and containers can use the RUNCOMFY_TOKEN environment variable.

faq.question: How do I find a model input schema?
faq.answer: Open the model catalog and inspect the API tab for the selected endpoint.

faq.question: Can I submit a job without waiting?
faq.answer: Yes. Use deferred execution, retain the request identifier, and check status later.

faq.question: Where are generated files saved?
faq.answer: Results use the current directory by default, or a directory selected for the request.

faq.question: Does the skill send data to an external service?
faq.answer: Yes. Prompts, model inputs, and credentials are sent to RunComfy over its documented network endpoints.
